Control your connected **Philips air purifiers and humidifiers** from Gladys, on your local network, without
the Philips cloud: air quality (PM2.5, allergen index, humidity), modes and fan speed, target humidity, child
lock, display light, and the hours left on each filter. Changes made on the purifier or in the Philips app
show up in Gladys within seconds.

> **Developed without the hardware: feedback welcome.** This integration was written from the protocol as
> documented by the open-source community, and tested against a simulated purifier. If your model behaves
> differently, open an issue at https://github.com/guim31/gladys-philips-air/issues with the output of the
> probe script (see Troubleshooting).
>
> Not affiliated with Philips or Versuni. Philips is a trademark of Koninklijke Philips N.V.

## Requirements

- Gladys Assistant 5.1 or later.
- A Philips purifier or humidifier with Wi-Fi that speaks the local **CoAP** protocol (UDP port 5683): the
  AC series (AC2889, AC2729, AC3829, AC3858, AC4236, Series 2000i and 3000i…), the newer AC0850, AC0950,
  AC2220, AC3220, AC3420, AC4220, and the HU humidifiers (HU1509, HU4209, HU5710…). The full list is under
  "Supported models".
- The purifier set up once in the **Philips Air+** app (it joins your Wi-Fi there), on the same local network
  as Gladys.
- Its **IP address**. Your router lists it (the device often appears as `MXCHIP…`). Give it a fixed address
  (DHCP reservation) in your router: the integration finds the purifier at the address you enter.

## Configuration

In Gladys, open **Integrations → Philips Air → Configuration**:

| Field                         | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| IP addresses of the purifiers | One or more IPv4 addresses, separated by commas.                                                                                                                                                 |
| Refresh interval              | How often each purifier is read (10 s to 2 min, 30 s by default). Changes are usually pushed at once by the purifier; this read is the safety net.                                               |
| Filter replacement warning    | When the maintenance trigger fires for a filter to replace: when the purifier asks (default), or 1 day, 3 days, 1 week before. The pre-filter is always announced when the purifier asks for it. |
| Language of the device names  | Language of the names given to new devices, their features, the mode list and the trigger messages. French by default.                                                                           |

Save, then open the **Discovery** tab: one device per purifier, named after the name it has in the Philips
app and its model, for example `Bedroom (AC2729/10)`. Add it to Gladys.

The **Check the purifiers** button (Configuration screen) reads every address at once and tells which
purifiers answer, and which model is not in the list of the integration.

## The device

Each purifier gets only the features its model has:

| Feature                    | In Gladys                                                                         |
| -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Power                      | On/off switch.                                                                    |
| Mode                       | List of the modes of the model (see below).                                       |
| Fan speed                  | Manual speed, 1 to 2, 3 or 5 depending on the model. Setting it selects "Manual". |
| PM2.5                      | Fine particles, in µg/m³.                                                         |
| Allergen index             | Philips indoor allergen index, 1 (good) to 12 (very poor).                        |
| Humidity                   | Relative humidity, in % (models with a humidity sensor).                          |
| Temperature                | In °C (models with a temperature sensor).                                         |
| Target humidity            | List of the targets the humidifier accepts (40 to 70 %, or 30 to 70 %).           |
| Humidification             | Switches the humidifier part of a 2-in-1 purifier on or off.                      |
| Water tank                 | "Low" when the tank is empty or removed, "Normal" otherwise.                      |
| Child lock                 | Locks the buttons of the purifier.                                                |
| Display light              | Brightness of the display and the air quality ring.                               |
| Pre-filter (hours left)    | Hours before the pre-filter needs cleaning.                                       |
| HEPA filter (hours left)   | Hours before the HEPA (or NanoProtect) filter needs replacing.                    |
| Carbon filter (hours left) | Hours before the active carbon filter needs replacing.                            |
| Wick (hours left)          | Hours before the humidifier wick needs replacing.                                 |

### Modes

Depending on the model: **Auto**, **Allergen**, **Bacteria and virus**, **Pollution**, **Gentle**,
**Medium**, **High**, **Sleep**, **Allergy sleep**, **Turbo**, and **Manual** (a fixed fan speed). Choosing a
mode also switches the purifier on. A model missing from the list of the integration still gets its
sensors, its power switch and its filters, but no mode list.

## Dashboard widget

The **Philips purifier** widget shows, for the purifier chosen in its settings:

- PM2.5 and humidity, live;
- the mode, the allergen index on the Philips scale (Good, Fair, Poor, Very poor), the running boost and its
  end time, and what the purifier asks for (or the filter closest to its end);
- buttons: two usual modes (Auto or Pollution, Sleep), **Boost** for 15, 30 or 60 minutes (widget setting),
  and on/off.

## Scene trigger

**Purifier maintenance needed** fires once when a purifier starts asking for care, and again only after it
was done (filter replaced, tank refilled):

- Pre-filter to clean (when the purifier asks for it);
- HEPA filter to replace, Carbon filter to replace, Wick to replace (when the purifier asks, or earlier: see
  the "Filter replacement warning" setting);
- Water tank empty (while humidifying).

Filters: the purifier, and the items you care about. Variables: `item`, `hours_left`, and `message`, a
ready-made text such as "Bedroom (AC2729/10): HEPA filter to replace (70 h left)" in the language of the
configuration.

## Scene action

**Boost the purifier** runs the purifier in Turbo (or at its highest speed) for 5 to 240 minutes, then puts
it back in the mode it had, or switches it off if it was off. If someone changes the purifier during the
boost, the boost ends without touching it. The action outputs `until`, the end of the boost.

## Scene examples

- **After cooking**: when the kitchen PM2.5 goes above 35 µg/m³, **Boost the purifier** for 20 minutes.
- **Filter reminder**: on **Purifier maintenance needed**, send `{{triggerEvent.data.message}}` to your phone.
- **Night**: at 10:30 pm, set the bedroom purifier mode to **Sleep** and its display light to Off; at 7 am,
  back to **Auto**.
- **Away**: when the house is empty, switch the purifiers to **Auto**; when the first person comes home,
  **Boost the purifier** for 15 minutes.

## Troubleshooting

- **"No Philips purifier answers"**: check the IP address (it may have changed: give it a fixed one), that
  the purifier is plugged in and on Wi-Fi, and that it answers in the Philips app. A strict firewall on the
  Gladys machine (ufw…) can block the UDP traffic between the integration container and your network.
- **It worked, then stopped answering**: the firmware of these purifiers is known to stop answering local
  requests after a while (also seen with Home Assistant). Unplug the purifier for 10 seconds; the
  integration reconnects by itself.
- **A model without the mode list**: your model is not in the list yet. Run the probe script from a computer
  on the same network, `node scripts/probe.mjs <IP address>` (in a clone of the repository, Node.js 22+): it
  only reads, and masks the identifiers. Paste its output in an issue.
- **More details**: the logs of the integration (Gladys → Integrations → Philips Air → Logs) only show the
  life of the purifiers at the normal level; set `LOG_LEVEL=debug` on the container for every read.

## Limits

- Local control only (CoAP over UDP 5683). The older models that only speak HTTP, and the newest firmware that
  closed the local access, are not supported.
- No automatic discovery: the purifiers do not announce themselves in a way the Gladys container can see. Enter
  their IP address.
- Mode lists come from what the open-source community observed; a model may accept a mode its list does not
  show, or the reverse. Timers, beep, ambient light and the "preferred index" of some models are not
  exposed.
- The pushed changes go through the Docker network of Gladys; when they do not, the next read (30 s by
  default) brings them.
- A boost in progress survives a restart of the integration, but ends at the next answer if the purifier was
  away when it was due.

## Supported models

- AC series, classic firmware: AC2729, AC2889, AC2936, AC2939, AC2958, AC2959, AC3021, AC3033, AC3036,
  AC3039, AC3055, AC3059, AC3259, AC3829, AC3854/50, AC3854/51, AC3858/50, AC3858/51, AC3858/83, AC3858/86,
  AC4231, AC4236, AC5659, AC5660.
- AC1715 and AC0850 (firmware "AWS_Philips_AIR").
- New generation: AC0850 (firmware "AWS_Philips_AIR_Combo"), AC0950, AC0951, AC2210, AC2220, AC2221, AC3210,
  AC3220, AC3221, AC3420, AC3421, AC4220, AC4221.
- Humidifiers: HU1509, HU1510, HU4209, HU4210, HU5710.

Other models of these generations get their sensors, power and filters.

## Configuration settings

These are the settings Philips Air asks for in its configuration screen in Gladys.

| Setting | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Connecting your purifiers | `section` | No | Gladys talks to Philips purifiers on your local network, without the Philips cloud. Set up the purifier in the Philips Air+ app first, then enter its IP address below (a fixed address in your router is best). Not affiliated with Philips or Versuni. |
| IP addresses of the purifiers | `string` | No | Separated by commas. Your router lists them (the device is often named "MXCHIP"). |
| Refresh interval | `select` | No | How often each purifier is read. Changes are usually pushed at once; this read is the safety net. |
| Filter replacement warning | `select` | No | When the "Maintenance needed" trigger fires for a filter to replace (HEPA, carbon, wick). The pre-filter is announced when the purifier asks. |
| Language of the device names | `select` | No | Names given to new devices, their features, the mode list and the trigger messages. |

## How to install Philips Air in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: Philips Air appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/guim31/gladys-philips-air:1.0.1`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/guim31/gladys-philips-air](https://github.com/guim31/gladys-philips-air).

Philips Air requires Gladys `>=5.1.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.
